bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Cyclicality of the real estate industry — Management states the real estate industry is cyclical in nature and any downturn can impact the Company's performance; presence in both residential and industrial segments plus a premium/mid-premium focus is cited as the key mitigant, with the premium segment described as relatively more resilient than luxury.
- Commodity cost inflation and geopolitical disruption of construction inputs — Inflation in commodity costs can impact profitability. Geopolitical events can influence energy prices and the cost of steel, cement, aluminium, glass and tiles, and supply disruptions particularly in aluminium and tiles may lead to cost pressures; mitigated through cost-escalation provisions, value engineering, long-term/forward contracts and price revisions.
- Sales risk - inability to sell projects as per plan — Listed as a key operational risk; residential revenue depends on absorption of launched and sustenance inventory, and market volatility can influence homebuyer sentiment given the high-value nature of residential purchases.
- Execution and delivery risk leading to cost overruns — Inability to complete and deliver projects within timelines is flagged as a key operational risk, alongside difficulties in appointment and retention of contractors and manpower; addressed through a structured control framework with assigned ownership.
- Talent attraction, retention and attrition — Inability to attract and retain talent is an explicit operational risk; permanent-employee turnover disclosed in the BRSR at 20.85% (IC&IC) and 18.79% (Residential) for FY 2025-26, with IC&IC turnover higher than the prior year.
- Fraud, unethical practices and non-compliance with laws and regulations — Flagged as an operational risk that can lead to penalties and litigation; managed through corporate governance policies, a Code of Conduct for all associates, an ethics helpline and whistle-blower mechanism routed to the Business Ethics & Governance Committee or the Audit Committee Chairperson.
- Cybersecurity and AI-driven vulnerability exposure — Management explicitly cites increased exposure to security breaches and exploitation of vulnerabilities driven by rapid advancements in AI as an operational risk.
- Policy and regulatory risk, including approval delays for land acquisition and development — The sector remains sensitive to changes in government policy; procedural delays in approvals related to land acquisition and development are described as a structural challenge and unfavourable regulatory changes may impact business performance; mitigated by disciplined land acquisition with thorough due diligence.
- Interest-rate and affordability sensitivity of residential demand — Management believes domestic interest rates, particularly repo rates, have a greater bearing on residential demand and affordability than global rate movements; stability in repo rates has been supportive, implying demand sensitivity if that reverses.
- Supply chain management (BRSR material issue) — Identified in the BRSR material responsible business conduct issues table as both a risk and an opportunity, driven by changing customer behaviour, higher Scope 3 emissions and potential work stoppage due to unethical operations in the supply chain.
- Business concentration in a single activity and a narrow set of geographies — BRSR discloses 100% of turnover from construction (residential >98% of turnover), with residential operations in only four states (Maharashtra, Haryana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu) and IC&IC in three (Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Gujarat), and no export contribution - concentrating exposure to Indian urban real estate cycles.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Scale the business under a stated 14X growth ambition for the decade, of which 5X has been delivered in the last 6 years, anchored in disciplined execution, financial prudence and long-term value creation.
- Premiumisation as the next chapter of growth - shift the residential portfolio towards premium/mid-premium products with better locations, modern facades, larger 2/3/4 BHK typologies and differentiated amenities, while gradually reducing affordable-segment exposure.
- Deepen presence in high-potential micro-markets and core cities - MMR, Pune, Bengaluru and Chennai - including entry into Mumbai's redevelopment segment and mixed-use ecosystems.
- Balance outright land acquisition with asset-light models (joint developments, society and cluster redevelopment) to support capital efficiency and scalability.
- Shift the sales mix over the next five years towards sustenance projects (from 60% new launches / 40% sustenance today to 25% new launches / 75% sustenance).
- Use partnerships as a growth pillar - the joint venture with Mitsui Fudosan Group, Japan's largest residential developer, being operationalised through the first joint project Mahindra Blossom in Bengaluru.
- In IC&IC, maximise value creation from existing locations, enhance infrastructure readiness and occupancy, monetise land parcels through sale/lease and resolve legacy land aggregation/approval/litigation issues to create further pipeline.
- Sustainability as a core product differentiator - 100% green portfolio maintained and all new developments to be Net Zero by 2030, aligned to the Mahindra Group 'Planet Positive' vision.
- Financial prudence with clear return thresholds, disciplined capital deployment and maintenance of balance sheet strength while scaling.
- Customer-experience and execution focus - sharp CX across touchpoints, QCT initiatives and governance mechanisms, digital monitoring tools, and digital/channel-led sales with an expanded channel-partner ecosystem.
- Invest in leadership development, brand building, sustainability and digital capabilities including efficiencies driven by AI.
- Dividends are governed by a Dividend Distribution Policy framed under Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations, attached to the Annual Report and published on the Company's website; the Board declares dividend in accordance with the principles and criteria set out in that policy and Section 123(1) of the Companies Act, 2013. For FY 2025-26 the Board recommended a final dividend of Rs 3.50 per equity share (35% of face value), up from Rs 2.80 per share (28% of face value) in the prior year, payable out of past profits (retained earnings), and decided not to transfer any amount to the General Reserve, with the balance proposed to be retained in the Profit and Loss Account - i.e. earnings are largely retained to fund project development, land acquisition and the execution pipeline. Board-level oversight of capital allocation is explicitly linked to the double-materiality assessment, which the Company states informs its Enterprise Risk Management framework, climate-scenario analysis, capital allocation decisions and its six strategic pillars.
- Commitment to make all new developments Net Zero by 2030 while maintaining a 100% green certified portfolio; the Company reports India's first three Net Zero Energy and first two Net Zero Waste residential developments.
- All residential construction is of 100% green certified buildings - BRSR reports this as the description of the main business activity accounting for 100% of turnover.
- Publishing its 4th Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report, developed in accordance with SEBI guidelines and the nine principles of the National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct, on a consolidated reporting boundary.
- CSR intervention areas: environmental stewardship (afforestation, water conservation, renewable and energy-efficient infrastructure), education and skill development (including girl-child education and differently-abled students), women empowerment and livelihood creation, health and community well-being, and community infrastructure and social development.
- During the year the Company and its subsidiaries incurred a CSR expenditure of Rs 524 lakhs and positively impacted more than 30,000 beneficiaries across their operational geographies, with employee volunteering an integral part of the CSR approach.
- Reduction of Scope 3 emissions through supply chain management is identified as a material responsible business conduct issue, with an approach of aligning suppliers/contractors to company standards.
- Structured grievance redressal across stakeholder groups - a third-party Ethics Helpline and whistle-blower route for employees and contractors/suppliers, Customer Assist / M Life app / facility-management helpdesk for customers, on-site complaint registers for workers and in-person reporting for communities.
- Risk Management Committee of four members - one Non-Executive Director, one Independent Director, the MD & CEO and the CFO - responsible for the risk management policy and business continuity plan, with the Board also reviewing risks regularly.
- Continued focus on sustainable and environment-friendly practices is stated as supporting compliance with evolving environmental regulations.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: MLDL describes FY 2025-26 as a phase of strong expansion driven by strategic land acquisitions across its portfolio, laying the foundation for its next phase of scaling up. Gross Development Value (GDV) additions of Rs 18,060 Cr were made during the year through selective land acquisitions and business development initiatives across key markets including Mumbai, Pune and Bengaluru - in line with the FY 2024-25 GDV, which had included a Thane unlock of Rs 7,500 Cr - with management stating this consistency over two consecutive years positions the Company for future growth and enhances long-term visibility of the growth roadmap. Expansion during the year was executed through new residential launches including Mahindra NewHaven, Mahindra Marina64 and Mahindra Blossom, alongside sustenance sales at Mahindra Vista, Mahindra IvyLush, Mahindra Citadel and Mahindra Lakewoods. Looking ahead, the Company has set out a 14X growth ambition for the decade with a stated roadmap to scale both the residential and Integrated Cities & Industrial Clusters (IC&IC) businesses while maintaining balance sheet strength; in IC&IC the intent is to keep building high-quality industrial ecosystems while steadily unlocking value from the existing land bank over time. Supporting investments are directed at leadership development, brand building, sustainability initiatives and digital capabilities including AI-driven efficiencies. No rupee capex budget, plant capacity addition or commissioning schedule is disclosed in this section - the business is land- and project-led rather than plant-based.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Premiumisation is reshaping residential demand - the affordable segment's volume share has declined from 48% to 17% over five years while premium/mid-premium grew from 46% to 69% and luxury more than doubled from 6% to 14%, with premiumisation continuing to drive pricing growth.
- Consolidation towards organised and credible developers post RERA, GST and the insolvency framework - organised share expected to rise from 23% in 2021 to an estimated 40-50% by 2030.
- Sustained income growth - lower-mid and upper-mid income households projected to grow from 54% in 2018 to 78% by 2030.
- Larger unit sizes as consumer preferences evolve - average unit size up 40% in four years, from 1,180 sq.ft. in 2021 to 1,657 sq.ft. in 2025, driven by post-pandemic demand for work-from-home spaces, balconies and open areas.
- Near-term moderation in sales visible in 2025 due to a lag in approvals and launches, but underlying demand fundamentals described as intact.
- Industrial real estate entering policy-backed expansion - manufacturing FDI into India up from US$ 8 bn in 2016 to US$ 19 bn in 2025, manufacturing share of GDP set to rise from 17% to 25% by 2030, PLI schemes worth Rs 1.9 lakh Cr across 14 sectors, Rs 2,500 Cr for plug-and-play industrial parks and a Rs 10,000 Cr SME growth fund.
- Structural shift in global supply chains and India's positioning as a preferred manufacturing destination supporting long-term interest in the Company's industrial parks.
- Macro backdrop - real GDP estimated to grow 7.4% in FY 2025-26 with construction activity registering healthy growth (approximately 7.0%).
- Demand for integrated industrial ecosystems remains steady, driven by manufacturing, logistics, engineering and technology-led sectors, with leasing supported by a mix of expansion from existing tenants and new customer acquisitions.
- Residential demand supported by branded, well-executed developments in premium/mid-premium segments, healthy end-user participation and a robust channel-partner ecosystem.
- Total development footprint of 53.65 msft as on 31 March 2026, comprising completed development of 25.16 msft, total ongoing projects of 13.83 msft (7.58 msft area sold, 4.41 msft current inventory, 1.84 msft future phases) and pipeline projects (excluding strategic projects) of 14.66 msft.
- Gross Development Value (GDV) additions of Rs 18,060 Cr in FY 2025-26, driven by selective land acquisitions and business development across Mumbai, Pune and Bengaluru - in line with FY 2024-25 GDV (which included a Thane unlock of Rs 7,500 Cr).
- Upcoming project pipeline concentrated in high-demand micro-markets, largely Mumbai redevelopment plus select Bengaluru and NCR corridors - Lokhandwala 2 (Mumbai, 2.22 acres, cluster redevelopment), Mulund (Mumbai, 3.08 acres, society redevelopment), Navrat 2 (Bengaluru, 8.79 acres, outright acquisition of shares), Chembur (Mumbai, 4.4 acres, society redevelopment), Mahalunge (Pune, 13.46 acres, outright), Navy 2 (Mumbai, 1.65 acres, society redevelopment), Matunga (Mumbai, 1.54 acres, cluster redevelopment) and Thane (own land, DP plan approved in FY26).
- Land pipeline strengthened during the year with continued focus on redevelopment and joint development opportunities in key urban markets, reinforcing long-term visibility of growth.
- In IC&IC, an additional 100 acres was unlocked at Origins by Mahindra, Chennai, of which 60 acres was sold within three months.

currentContext.expansion: MLDL describes FY 2025-26 as a phase of strong expansion driven by strategic land acquisitions across its portfolio, laying the foundation for its next phase of scaling up. Gross Development Value (GDV) additions of Rs 18,060 Cr were made during the year through selective land acquisitions and business development initiatives across key markets including Mumbai, Pune and Bengaluru - in line with the FY 2024-25 GDV, which had included a Thane unlock of Rs 7,500 Cr - with management stating this consistency over two consecutive years positions the Company for future growth and enhances long-term visibility of the growth roadmap. Expansion during the year was executed through new residential launches including Mahindra NewHaven, Mahindra Marina64 and Mahindra Blossom, alongside sustenance sales at Mahindra Vista, Mahindra IvyLush, Mahindra Citadel and Mahindra Lakewoods. Looking ahead, the Company has set out a 14X growth ambition for the decade with a stated roadmap to scale both the residential and Integrated Cities & Industrial Clusters (IC&IC) businesses while maintaining balance sheet strength; in IC&IC the intent is to keep building high-quality industrial ecosystems while steadily unlocking value from the existing land bank over time. Supporting investments are directed at leadership development, brand building, sustainability initiatives and digital capabilities including AI-driven efficiencies. No rupee capex budget, plant capacity addition or commissioning schedule is disclosed in this section - the business is land- and project-led rather than plant-based.

one-line thesis: Mahindra Lifespace reported a sharp turnaround to Rs 109 Cr PAT in Q3FY26 driven by critical OCs and robust IC leasing, validating the post-rights issue balance sheet strength. The successful Rs 1,000 Cr+ weekend sale of 'Blossom' and 50% leasing of new industrial acreage within 30 days demonstrate strong brand pull in the premium mid-market despite broader luxury slowdowns.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Not explicitly stated (PAT Rs 109 Cr Q3, Rs 208 Cr 9M); EBITDA/Margin: IC margins trending up, Residential ~10% net margin on completed projects; PAT: Rs 109 Cr (Q3) vs -Rs 23 Cr (Q3LY), Rs 208 Cr (9M) vs -Rs 24 Cr (9M LY); Order Book: GDV inventory ~Rs 4,700 Cr executable, Total GDV pipeline Rs 47,000 Cr; Net Debt: Negative NDE (-0.12), Cash Rs 724 Cr. One-offs: PAT surge driven by timing of 6 OCs received in last 45 days (Eden, Nestalgia, Happinest).
guidance: Revenue Growth: Implicit strong growth via OC conversion; Margin: Targeting ~10%+ residential net margins; Order Inflow: FY27 pre-sales guidance Rs 4,500-5,000 Cr; Capex/Commissioning: Focus on Tier-1 vendor partnerships to scale execution without heavy capex.
order book & pipeline: Current Inventory GDV ~Rs 1,800 Cr (includes Blossom); Future Phases GDV ~Rs 2,600 Cr; Total Executable GDV ~Rs 4,700 Cr; Long-term Pipeline GDV Rs 47,000 Cr (Resi Rs 9,500 Cr + IC Rs 500 Cr near-term targets).
segment / subsidiary detail: Residential: Q3 Pre-sales Rs 572 Cr (9M Rs 1,773 Cr); Collections Rs 1,472 Cr (9M). IC: Leasing up 30% (9M), 53 Cr sq ft leased vs 47 Cr prior; Origins 2A (Chennai) 50% leased in 30 days. New Wins: Lokmanya Tilak Nagar redevelopment (~Rs 1,000 Cr GDV).
growth verticals / optionality: IC Business: 1,520 acres potential value Rs 5,000-6,000 Cr (PAT ~Rs 1,500 Cr) over 10 years; Pipeline Projects: Matunga, Chembur, Thane, Jaipur (Pink City), Murud; Society Redevelopment: Lokhandwala (design phase), Sai Baba (launch Q2FY27).
margins & cost dynamics: Residential net margins ~10% on recent completions; IC margins expanding due to higher realization; Cost of Debt reduced to 6.7% (from 8.9% YoY) post-rights issue debt paydown.
capex / expansion: Asset-light execution model; Scaling via Tier-1/1.5 contractor partnerships rather than balance sheet heavy capex; Investment in digital systems for quality/snagging and talent acquisition.
capital allocation: Rights Issue proceeds utilized to repay Rs 918 Cr long-term debt; Net cash position (Negative NDE); Focus on land acquisition in core markets (Mumbai, Pune, Bangalore) via JVs/redevelopment.
risks & watch-items: Regulatory Delays: EC requirement causing temporary RERA launch delays (one-time correction); Market Slowdown: Luxury segment (Rs 7-10 Cr+) showing weakness in NCR/Mumbai; Inventory Overhang: Industry-wide increase to 15 months.
management quality / tone: Confident and Execution-Focused; Highlighting 'buoyancy' in demand for premium mid-market; Emphasis on de-risking delivery via vendor upgrades and culture shift.
non-obvious takeaways: IC business acts as a 'plotted' revenue stream similar to peers' residential plotted sales, providing early cash flow; The 'one-time' regulatory friction (EC before CC) artificially suppressed Q3 launches but created a pent-up supply for Q4/FY27; Management explicitly avoiding the 'luxury' trap (Rs 10 Cr+) to maintain velocity.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Premiumisation is reshaping residential demand - the affordable segment's volume share has declined from 48% to 17% over five years while premium/mid-premium grew from 46% to 69% and luxury more than doubled from 6% to 14%, with premiumisation continuing to drive pricing growth.
- Consolidation towards organised and credible developers post RERA, GST and the insolvency framework - organised share expected to rise from 23% in 2021 to an estimated 40-50% by 2030.
- Sustained income growth - lower-mid and upper-mid income households projected to grow from 54% in 2018 to 78% by 2030.
- Larger unit sizes as consumer preferences evolve - average unit size up 40% in four years, from 1,180 sq.ft. in 2021 to 1,657 sq.ft. in 2025, driven by post-pandemic demand for work-from-home spaces, balconies and open areas.
- Near-term moderation in sales visible in 2025 due to a lag in approvals and launches, but underlying demand fundamentals described as intact.
- Industrial real estate entering policy-backed expansion - manufacturing FDI into India up from US$ 8 bn in 2016 to US$ 19 bn in 2025, manufacturing share of GDP set to rise from 17% to 25% by 2030, PLI schemes worth Rs 1.9 lakh Cr across 14 sectors, Rs 2,500 Cr for plug-and-play industrial parks and a Rs 10,000 Cr SME growth fund.
- Structural shift in global supply chains and India's positioning as a preferred manufacturing destination supporting long-term interest in the Company's industrial parks.
- Macro backdrop - real GDP estimated to grow 7.4% in FY 2025-26 with construction activity registering healthy growth (approximately 7.0%).
- Demand for integrated industrial ecosystems remains steady, driven by manufacturing, logistics, engineering and technology-led sectors, with leasing supported by a mix of expansion from existing tenants and new customer acquisitions.
- Residential demand supported by branded, well-executed developments in premium/mid-premium segments, healthy end-user participation and a robust channel-partner ecosystem.
- Total development footprint of 53.65 msft as on 31 March 2026, comprising completed development of 25.16 msft, total ongoing projects of 13.83 msft (7.58 msft area sold, 4.41 msft current inventory, 1.84 msft future phases) and pipeline projects (excluding strategic projects) of 14.66 msft.
- Gross Development Value (GDV) additions of Rs 18,060 Cr in FY 2025-26, driven by selective land acquisitions and business development across Mumbai, Pune and Bengaluru - in line with FY 2024-25 GDV (which included a Thane unlock of Rs 7,500 Cr).
- Upcoming project pipeline concentrated in high-demand micro-markets, largely Mumbai redevelopment plus select Bengaluru and NCR corridors - Lokhandwala 2 (Mumbai, 2.22 acres, cluster redevelopment), Mulund (Mumbai, 3.08 acres, society redevelopment), Navrat 2 (Bengaluru, 8.79 acres, outright acquisition of shares), Chembur (Mumbai, 4.4 acres, society redevelopment), Mahalunge (Pune, 13.46 acres, outright), Navy 2 (Mumbai, 1.65 acres, society redevelopment), Matunga (Mumbai, 1.54 acres, cluster redevelopment) and Thane (own land, DP plan approved in FY26).
- Land pipeline strengthened during the year with continued focus on redevelopment and joint development opportunities in key urban markets, reinforcing long-term visibility of growth.
- In IC&IC, an additional 100 acres was unlocked at Origins by Mahindra, Chennai, of which 60 acres was sold within three months.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: MLDL describes FY 2025-26 as a phase of strong expansion driven by strategic land acquisitions across its portfolio, laying the foundation for its next phase of scaling up. Gross Development Value (GDV) additions of Rs 18,060 Cr were made during the year through selective land acquisitions and business development initiatives across key markets including Mumbai, Pune and Bengaluru - in line with the FY 2024-25 GDV, which had included a Thane unlock of Rs 7,500 Cr - with management stating this consistency over two consecutive years positions the Company for future growth and enhances long-term visibility of the growth roadmap. Expansion during the year was executed through new residential launches including Mahindra NewHaven, Mahindra Marina64 and Mahindra Blossom, alongside sustenance sales at Mahindra Vista, Mahindra IvyLush, Mahindra Citadel and Mahindra Lakewoods. Looking ahead, the Company has set out a 14X growth ambition for the decade with a stated roadmap to scale both the residential and Integrated Cities & Industrial Clusters (IC&IC) businesses while maintaining balance sheet strength; in IC&IC the intent is to keep building high-quality industrial ecosystems while steadily unlocking value from the existing land bank over time. Supporting investments are directed at leadership development, brand building, sustainability initiatives and digital capabilities including AI-driven efficiencies. No rupee capex budget, plant capacity addition or commissioning schedule is disclosed in this section - the business is land- and project-led rather than plant-based.

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.
